tldr: Deep research agents are being redefined by what they read and how they search. In October, an arXiv paper proposed an iterative, state-centric agent for literature research, and another introduced a benchmark for reports centered on a source video.
whats_new: On Nov 2, DR Pixel proposed page-native deep research: vision-language models read papers as page images, rather than OCR-extracted text.
why_it_matters: Text-only retrieval pipelines drop tables, figures and equations; if your research agent ingests PDFs, the input modality is now a design choice to test.

status.detail: Academic work is widening deep research from text search to iterative state, video sources and page images.

beats.headline: Optimist Deep Research tracks evolving understanding across literature search
beats.summary: Argues single-step retrieval plus summarization misses how an investigator's question changes.

beats.headline: A benchmark for video-centered deep research reports
beats.summary: Evaluates agents given a source video rather than a text query.

beats.headline: DR Pixel reads papers as page images with vision-language models
beats.summary: Targets tables, figures and equations lost to OCR text extraction.

open_questions: Does DR Pixel beat OCR-text baselines on figure- and table-heavy questions, and at what compute cost?
Do the video-centered and page-native benchmarks converge on a shared evaluation protocol?
Does iterative state tracking (Optimist) improve results on open-ended reports versus single-pass retrieval?
take_for_builders: If your research agent reads PDFs, test a vision-language pass on pages with tables and equations against your OCR pipeline before trusting text-only extraction.

day_captions.45845d76a34385a2: Treats literature research as iterative, with agent state updated as understanding of the question changes.
day_captions.ed508b2931c601f2: Introduces a benchmark task where the research report is centered on a given source video.
day_captions.2e1dfcc99bc4c300: Replaces OCR-extracted paper text with page-level vision-language input for deep research.
